endorsements.quote: Progress therefore depends on harmonized disclosure and auditable methods that let health systems judge whether AI genuinely improves care without shifting costs to other people or places.

unlisted_practices: Add AI-specific carbon disclosure clauses to digital health vendor contracts requiring model-level emissions data (training, retraining, and inference energy use) and data-center carbon intensity.
Include cradle-to-grave carbon emission factors for AI hardware (GPUs, servers, cooling equipment) in procurement templates and Scope 3 reporting.
Extend NHS Green Plans to include a full life-cycle assessment of AI hardware.
Set up lightweight monitoring of staff use of external generative AI tools, such as browser or network logging multiplied by an agreed emission factor, while weighing privacy concerns.
Develop an open, shared database of carbon factors for digital health and standardize how the carbon impact of digital interventions including AI is calculated.
Conduct robust pre-implementation and post-implementation carbon assessments of new health technologies including AI.

screen.reason: This paper analyzes current carbon reporting guidelines in the NHS and proposes governance, accounting, and procurement measures/recommendations to capture AI-related emissions.
